title.narrative: Peruvian Amazon Eco Bio Business Facility (Amazon EBBF)

description.narrative:
COMPONENT 1: Consolidation of the main pillars of REDD+
1.1. Strengthen the National Forest Monitoring System:
Forest Cover Monitoring Module (MMCB) of MINAM (available from 2001 to 2018, soon 2019) and the Land Use Change maps, developed for specific periods, produce country´s official deforestation information that has supported public financing for REDD+ pillars. Obtaining official deforestation data is a significant progress, however it is necessary to consolidate its methods to monitor forest loss and change land use.
To consolidate the current MMCB´s work, Peru needs to approach methodologically and technically secondary forest degradation measurement - since they have been developing disjointedly - besides new technology development for this measurement. This will improve the monitoring process and results, while reducing technical inconsistencies.
To generate all this information, it is required a consolidation effort, interoperability, and project actions to allow a public, secure and democratic knowledge management of deforestation and degradation data, and generation of methodologies and validation for deforestation causes information, whose data can be institutionalized and validated. This work will involve development of capacities of public and private actors, involved in the deforestation supervision, to use protocols and databases and make political decisions to address deforestation causes in their regions.
1.2. Update the FREL:
The current FREL, approved in 2016 by the UNFCCC, covers emissions from deforestation in the Amazon biome. Near to its validity end it is necessary to develop, socialize and present a new FREL for a 2021 beginning period. Experts raised technical elements like the need of making a full uncertainties evaluation or to consider subsequent uses of land deforestation during the revision of the current version. Suggestions and compliance with existing RBP programs will be incorporated in this new document. This subcomponent´s activities will be complemented with ONUREDD support related work done to update forest data degradation for the new FREL scope expansion.
1.3 Address safeguards within REDD+ implementation:
Since 2017, Peru has a Safeguards Roadmap, implemented under a step-by-step approach. To date, there have been significant advances, like the National Safeguard Interpretation and the first Summary on REDD+ Safeguards information publication. Peru has also established the Technical Subcommittee on Safeguards, which brings together actors involved in the REDD+ safeguards issue, including indigenous peoples, state sectors, and NGOs. This space has collected compliance recommendations with a national safeguards approach development, and has laid the foundations to strengthen and achieve the full and effective participation of stakeholders.
Significant progress has been achieved but it is necessary to deepen actors and instruments strengthening and protocols and safeguards procedures development. Results will address: i) indigenous people, regional governments and private sectors strengthening capacities through participatory processes, workshops and guidelines, as they perform actively in safeguard compliance and oversight; and ii) the development and start-up of the Information Module on Safeguards and the Citizen Service Mechanism (MAC - complaints mechanism) at regional and national level.
As beneficiary of several Emission Reduction Programs (PCPF and DCI), it is important for Peru to present integrated safeguards compliance results to MIS, considering indicators of different donors.
COMPONENT 2: Avoid GHG emissions through eco bio-business models (EBB)
With GCF grant, Profonanpe will start a pilot scheme of blended finance to boost EBB models in the peruvian Amazon as an alternative to unlock business opportunities and to catalyse private capital investment. Reducing and transfer investment risks is attractive for highly risked businesses such as nature-based models. Under this component, alternatives and approaches for blended finance will pilot, replicate and scale innovative business models based on forest conservation and restoration with non-timber forest products and ecosystem services, contributing to CC mitigation by avoiding deforestation and degradation, and therefore reducing emissions of GHG, with the support of allied institutions: platforms to articulate investment funds, incubators and accelerators.
2.1. Fostering sustainable EBB models
Potential EBB related to Amazon forest restoration and sustainable use, for non-timber products, will be identified with the support of incubators (allies) to accompany and advise with specialized services and tools to start. Incubators will provide technical assistance and support for business plans (technical and financial feasibility), marketing, legal and management assistance. Another scenario includes current operating EBBs which will use accelerators (allies) services for market scale up. Finally, a specialized institution (allied) will match impact funds between donors and recipients.
Enabling conditions to attract private investors include: (i) reducing transaction costs for credible projects identification with scalable social and environmental impacts, (ii) matching an honest and transparent partner as a valuable asset for investors (“bond of trust”), (iii) developing methodologies, instruments and metrics to support communication zooming in environmental trends to investors, and (iv) clarifying the attribution gap related to a specific investment and its expected impacts.
This subcomponent´s expected result is the financial mechanism architecture creation and allies’ partnership construction to ensure viable financial and autonomous EBB. Government entities like PRODUCE, will also be involved as strategic allies.
2.2. Investment in EBB
Around 10 EBBs related to forest conservation and restoration, currently operating in the Peruvian Amazon, will be assisted by allied institutions, providing technical support and helping explore ecosystemic marketplaces.
Current EBB will be identified during FP design phase to assure their viability and potential for future reimbursement. Pro impact fund and specialized match investment platforms will help leverage additional incomes through a new financial mechanism. These reimbursable grants will be considered as seed capital, initial investment in exchange for an income´s percentage or bought shares, at their return it will be used to support forthcoming EBB fostered in sub component 2.1. Around US$ 450,000 reimbursable grant could be delivered for each EBB for these activities, expecting to perform at 1:1 ROI.
As well, there will be a call for proposals opportunity to generate innovative and scalable ideas and attract investment towards them in specialized impact funds platforms.
This subcomponent´s expected result is to increase the number of successful EBB with a regional, national and/or international market presence and its mitigation impacts in CC.
Several of the pre-identified Amazon forest EBB have more than ten years operating. Nonetheless, they have remained as small start-ups as obstacles describe in section B.1, with difficulties to upgrade to more efficient technologies and larger markets scales. This applies to similar EBB along the country. Therefore, the experience gained by leveraging these first set of EBB and by proving the work strategy through incubators and accelerators at larger scales, could be replicated in such other similar EBB identified in other regions or even applied to other related to products or services that could help adapt to CC. Furthermore, work done at the Ministry level will also facilitate the insertion scaling of new and diverse EBB.
With 27 years of experience, Profonanpe manages projects related to biodiversity conservation, mitigation and adaptation to CC, with resources from bilateral and multilateral cooperation, privates and others. Accredited by the Adaptation Fund and the GCF as a DAE for Peru, Profonanpe demonstrates its capacity to fulfil international standards related to project and financial management and to environmental, social and gender policies.
Throughout its projects, Profonanpe has delivered resources to NGOs, associations and communities, as subgrants or sub-projects for both project execution or EBB implementation. This experience will be applied in this proposal in order to ensure growth and success of the EBB supported by the project. Moreover, Profonanpe’s experience has always involved a joint work with public institutions at national and local level, which will also be the case for this proposal, more specific in regards with component 1.
Diagram schematizes of implementation arrangements in Annex 1.
The Steering Committee, is the higher decision level to approve annual operation plans (AOP), review the progress execution, provide recommendations and review the results of midterm and final external evaluation. Its composition will be further described during FP development.
To comply with GCF requirements, implementation arrangements consider a project team and project execution specific budget. The expenses include: (i) operational expenditures; (ii) safeguards implementation; (iii) communication development; (iv) monitoring; (v) midterm and final evaluation; (vi) auditing and others.
As part of the M&E, project team will prepare the annual report while Profonanpe will support them with its revision and subsequent submission to the GCF. Project team will directly coordinate with staff members within MINAM (component 1). Similarly, project team will coordinate with EBB representatives and allied institutions (incubators, accelerators, platforms) for component 2. Profonanpe’s technical direction will monitor technical and financial objectives advances, the Steering Committee will ensure transparency and accountability by reviewing and approving AOP and annual reports prepared by the project team. Description of Steering Committee´s functions and composition to be delivered in the FP.
An external audit company meeting GCF standards will prepare annual audit reports; and individual external expert consultants, the midterm and final evaluations. Finally, Profonanpe’s tools and procedures for internal control, external communications and safeguards, among others, will be available for the project use.
